claim: A standard 3-day Beijing itinerary groups Mutianyu Great Wall with Temple of Heaven on one day, Qianmen/Forbidden City/Tiananmen on another, and National Museum plus Summer Palace on a third.
quote: Day 1: Mutianyu Great Wall + Temple of Heaven; Day 2: Qianmen Street + Forbidden City + Tiananmen Square; Day 3: National Museum of China + Summer Palace

claim: Forbidden City, National Museum and Tiananmen Square require booking at least 7 days in advance; Summer Palace and Temple of Heaven at least 3 days ahead.
quote: The Forbidden City, National Museum of China and Tiananmen Square must be booked at least 7 days in advance, while Summer Palace and Temple of Heaven should be booked at least 3 days before going.

claim: Wangfujing is the top base for first-timers, about a 15-minute walk to the Forbidden City and Tiananmen with 5 subway lines, while Qianmen offers a cheaper, more traditional hutong base also within walking distance.
quote: About a 15-minute walk to the Forbidden City and Tiananmen; 5 subway lines pass through. Qianmen: Walking distance to Tiananmen Square and Forbidden City... Traditional Beijing feel, with hutongs, old shops, and local snacks

claim: The recommended Mutianyu sequence is depart Beijing by 7:30 AM to arrive 9:00-9:30, spend 2-3 hours walking the wall, descend by toboggan or cable car, and be back in the city by mid-afternoon.
quote: 7:30-8:30 AM: Depart Beijing; 9:00-9:30 AM: Arrive at Mutianyu; 9:30 AM-12:30 PM: Wall exploration; 12:30-1:30 PM: Lunch; 1:30-3:00 PM: Return to Beijing. A popular combination is 'chairlift up + toboggan down.'

claim: Mutianyu sits roughly 70 km and 1.5-2 hours' drive from central Beijing; tourist buses depart 8-10 AM and Didi runs around 200 RMB each way.
quote: Mutianyu is located only around 70 km from Beijing... BusDa offers reliable departures at 8:00 a.m., 9:00 a.m., 10:00 a.m... Didi is the most comfortable option, with costs around 200 RMB (~25€) one way

claim: Exit the Forbidden City via the northern Gate of Divine Prowess and walk 5 minutes to Jingshan Park, where a ~10-minute climb gives the classic panorama back over the palace roofs, best in late afternoon light.
quote: From the exit of the Forbidden City, Jingshan Park is just a 5 minute walk... The climb takes about 10 minutes. At the top, you get the classic view of the Forbidden City... Time your visit to the late afternoon

claim: A 2-day Beijing plan covers Tiananmen, Forbidden City, Temple of Heaven, Summer Palace, a Great Wall hike and a hutong rickshaw ride, but guides flag it as rushed and recommend 3+ days for a relaxed pace.
quote: A typical 2-day itinerary includes Tiananmen Square, the Forbidden City, the Temple of Heaven, the Summer Palace, a hike on the Badaling Great Wall, and a rickshaw ride through Hutong alleys... a 3 to 6-day tour is recommended

claim: Most visitors spend two to three hours inside the Forbidden City entering at the Meridian Gate (south) and exiting at the Gate of Divine Prowess (north), with up to four hours if exploring side courtyards.
quote: Most people spend two to three hours inside the Forbidden City, and if you explore the side courtyards and take your time, you can easily spend four hours.
